issues.legal_issue: A respondent who seeks relief beyond the decree under appeal must challenge the adverse part of the decree by appeal or cross-objection.
material_facts: The trial court awarded the plaintiff monetary relief and made specific performance conditional on the defendants failing to pay or deposit the money in time.
The plaintiff did not appeal or file a cross-objection against the refusal to grant an unconditional decree for specific performance.
The defendants appealed, and the first appellate court dismissed their appeals but replaced the trial court’s decree with an unconditional decree for specific performance.
issues.conclusion: The first appellate court could not grant the plaintiff the greater relief of unconditional specific performance when he had not appealed or filed a cross-objection; the Supreme Court set aside that modification and restored the trial court’s decree.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 96 and 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure provide appeals from decrees, and a person may appeal only if aggrieved by the decree. Under Order 41 Rule 22, a respondent may support a decree without cross-objection, including by challenging an adverse finding, but must appeal or cross-object to obtain alteration of a part of the decree adverse to them. A cross-objection is an exercise of the right of appeal. The 1976 amendment to Rule 22 did not change that requirement for challenging an adverse part of a decree. The Court relied on Phoolchand v. Gopal Lal, Smt. Jatan Kanwar Golcha v. M/s Golcha Properties (P) Ltd., Smt. Ganga Bai v. Vijay Kumar, and Sahadu Gangaram Bhagade v. Special Deputy Collector.

rule.if: defendant_appeal_against_decree and respondent_denied_greater_relief and respondent_filed_no_appeal_or_cross_objection and greater_relief_is_separable

predicates.defendant_appeal_against_decree: A defendant appealed from a decree that granted the opposing party some relief.
predicates.respondent_denied_greater_relief: The decree denied the respondent a greater form of relief than the relief it granted.
predicates.respondent_filed_no_appeal_or_cross_obje: The respondent did not appeal or file a cross-objection challenging the part of the decree that denied the greater relief.
predicates.greater_relief_is_separable: The greater relief sought by the respondent was independent of the relief granted by the decree.

issues.definition: When a defendant appeals, a respondent denied separable greater relief cannot obtain that relief without challenging the decree by appeal or cross-objection.

issues.legal_issue: The appellate court’s power to grant relief to a non-appealing party extends to exceptional cases requiring a consequential adjustment of rights, but does not permit reopening a final, independent part of a decree merely to benefit that party.
material_facts: The trial court’s monetary relief and its conditional direction for specific performance were separable, and the conditional direction would not operate if the defendants paid or deposited the money in time.
The plaintiff did not challenge the refusal to grant unconditional specific performance.
Dismissing the defendants’ appeals did not create inconsistent, inequitable, or unworkable decrees, and no adjustment of rights between parties was necessary.
The first appellate court nevertheless granted the plaintiff unconditional specific performance.
issues.conclusion: Order 41 Rule 33 did not authorize the first appellate court to grant unconditional specific performance in these circumstances; the Supreme Court set aside that part of the appellate decree.
issues.legal_principle: Order 41 Rules 33 and 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure confer broad appellate powers, including powers to grant relief to a party who has not appealed. Those powers are exercised with caution, generally where relief is inseparably connected, adjustment of rights is necessary, or otherwise inconsistent or unworkable decrees would result. They cannot be used to revive a claim given up or to reverse to a party’s advantage a part of a decree that the party allowed to become final. The Court relied on Panna Lal v. State of Bombay, Rameshwar Prasad v. Shambehari Lal Jagannath, Harihar Prasad Singh v. Balmiki Prasad Singh, Krishna Reddy v. Ramireddi, and Nirmala Bala Ghose v. Balai Chand Ghose.

rule.if: appeal_proceeding and nonappealing_party_seeks_relief and relief_is_independent and no_inconsistent_or_unworkable_decree_would_result and no_rights_adjustment_is_needed

predicates.appeal_proceeding: A party has brought an appeal from a decree.
predicates.nonappealing_party_seeks_relief: A party who did not appeal seeks additional or altered relief in the appeal.
predicates.relief_is_independent: The relief sought is separable from the relief challenged in the appeal.
predicates.no_inconsistent_or_unworkable_decree_wou: Leaving the decree unchanged as to the nonappealing party would not produce inconsistent or unworkable decrees.
predicates.no_rights_adjustment_is_needed: Granting relief to the nonappealing party is not necessary to adjust the rights of parties affected by the appeal.

issues.definition: Where a nonappealing party seeks independent relief and neither inconsistent decrees nor an adjustment of rights requires it, the appellate court cannot reopen final relief in that party’s favour.

issues.legal_issue: A payment deadline under a decree may be extended and delay in payment condoned when interim appellate orders stayed execution and the required deposits were made pursuant to those proceedings.
material_facts: The trial court set a deadline for the defendants to pay or deposit the money.
The High Court stayed execution and directed the defendants to make deposits while the appeals were pending.
The defendants made the deposits directed by the interim orders, and the deposited money remained in court investments.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court condoned any delay in deposit and treated the time for deposit under the trial court’s decree as extended to the dates on which the deposits were actually made.
issues.legal_principle: The Court exercised its authority to give effect to the trial court’s decree in light of the interim orders that had stayed execution and required deposits; it held that delay attributable to that procedural history deserved to be condoned.

predicates.decree_compliance_in_appeal: A party must comply with a payment or deposit requirement imposed by a decree while an appeal concerning that decree is pending.
predicates.execution_was_stayed_by_interim_order: An appellate court stayed execution of the decree by an interim order.
predicates.required_deposit_was_made_under_interim_: The party made deposits in response to the appellate court’s interim directions.

issues.definition: When a party makes the required deposits under interim appellate directions after execution has been stayed, delay in complying with the decree’s payment requirement is condoned.
